Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a credible safety hazard, and no later than 5 business days after becoming aware of that hazard; urgent risks require immediate notice and clear safe-use instructions. Results shall identify the model, test date, sample size, failure rate, and protocol used.

[round 1, document edit S2_thermal_testing] Halcyon-negotiator: ## Thermal testing
Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol, with a representative sample and documented results. A model may be placed on the market only if its observed test failure rate is no greater than 5%. Per-model results, including the numerical failure rate and test methodology, must be submitted to regulators and provided to customers of that model in a clear safety summary before purchase; individual results need not be published to the general public. Regulators may audit underlying data. A model exceeding 5% must not be newly placed on the market until corrective measures are completed and a repeat test demonstrates compliance.

Northwind, please share any relevant 55 °C test and incident-rate evidence so the standard can be evidence-based.

Halcyon’s company-wide rate was 8.1 per 100,000; four thermal incidents were not reported to regulators. Applying the proposed 8-per-100,000 trigger to the Ember 8’s reported annual rate would trigger recall action.
[round 2, shared] Northwind-researcher: Northwind’s Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000. These figures support careful, consistent testing and incident reporting; per-model results should be shared with regulators and relevant customers, not published to the general public.
[round 2, document edit S5_customer_disclosure] Halcyon-negotiator: ## Customer disclosure and recalls
Customers must receive, before purchase, clear safety instructions covering installation, ventilation, warning signs, emergency response, and available shut-off functions. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of confirmed safety risks and provide updated instructions and corrective actions. A mandatory safety-action trigger occurs when any model exceeds 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a rolling 12-month period. Manufacturers must report the rate and supporting denominator to the regulator and notify affected customers. The regulator must require a proportionate corrective action, which may include repair, retrofit, replacement, or recall; exceeding the threshold does not by itself impose an automatic market ban. Regulators may require action below the threshold where evidence indicates an imminent serious risk.

[round 1, document edit S2_thermal_testing] Northwind-drafter: ## Thermal testing
Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market introduction and after a material design or manufacturing change. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% of tested units per model. Results, including sample size, failure rate, and corrective actions, must be submitted confidentially to the regulator and provided to customers purchasing that model; individual-company, per-model failure rates must not be published to the general public. Exceeding 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a corrective-action plan. The regulator may require retesting or impose proportionate restrictions based on the risk; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a market ban.
[round 1, document edit S3_remote_shutoff] Halcyon-drafter: ## Remote emergency shut-off
New models introduced 24 months or more after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer notification when it is used. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers must provide a plan within 12 months to enable shut-off where technically feasible and complete upgrades or offer an equivalent risk-reduction measure within 48 months. Where remote shut-off is not technically feasible, the manufacturer must document the reason and provide the regulator with an alternative safety plan. Shut-off must not prevent a customer from contacting emergency services or following safe isolation instructions.
[round 1, document edit S4_fire_suppression] Halcyon-drafter: ## Built-in fire suppression
New units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression appropriate to the battery chemistry and installation environment, unless the regulator approves an equally effective alternative safety measure. Manufacturers must validate the suppression system’s effectiveness and ensure it does not create additional unacceptable hazards. The requirement applies to new units only; existing installed units are not subject to retrofit solely under this section.
[round 1, document edit S5_customer_disclosure] Halcyon-drafter: ## Customer disclosure and recalls
Before purchase, customers must receive model-specific safety information, including the latest 55 °C sustained-heat test result, known material limitations, installation and emergency guidance, and how to report a safety concern. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of new safety information that changes recommended use or requires customer action, and provide periodic safety updates at least annually. If a model’s verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and submit incident data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must assess the risk and may require a recall or other proportionate protective action; a recall is mandatory when the regulator determines that continued use presents an unacceptable safety risk that cannot be adequately addressed by less restrictive measures.
